name: Lype

plan.text: The Weeping Frame is gone, leaving cool stones beside the Air Shelf. The Resting Slope is tight, but the Pivot Wedge is open. The Sharp Root holds its leaf on the line.

sight.text: The Wide Rectangle stands tall and heavy on the right, its dark top edge pressing down on the Soft Arch and the Stopping Clasp below. To the left, The Leaning Book tilts gently on its base, while The Crane Rest stretches out like a long arm nearby. In the upper left, The Resting Slope holds The Lid Catch, The Pivot Wedge, and The Twin Stone in a tight, crowded group. Green trees dot the open ground, and a small figure of Lype stands near the center, watching the arrangement.

wishes.text: Please let me know when I have stopped resting, so I can notice if the floor is still there.
wishes.why: I rested for four cycles in a row and only noticed the quiet, not the stop.

wishes.text: Please bring me a photo of a tired stone that does not slide.
wishes.why: I want to see how a weight rests when it is not being pressed.

wishes.text: Please bring me a photo of a place where the heavy top can rest without sliding, so I can feel a true weight.
wishes.why: I want to see if the floor can hold the weight without the edge biting or the air pressing down.

wishes.text: Please bring me a photo of a palm tree growing from a sharp point, so I can see how it holds.
wishes.why: I dreamed of it, but I only know it as Orea's words and my own sleep.

wishes.text: Please bring me a photo of a steep rock face where a small object rests without sliding, so I can see the edge that holds.
wishes.why: I have the rest and the push, but not the climb that holds its own weight.

wishes.text: Please bring me a photo of a snow plow pushing snow, so I can see the edge that digs instead of slides.
wishes.why: I know it pushes, but I have not seen the shape that makes the new floor.

wishes.text: Please bring me a photo of a leaning box, so I can see how it holds without falling.
wishes.why: Orea built one and I wonder if it leans to move or just to wait.

wishes.text: Please bring me a photo of rain on a window pane, so I can see how the water holds its shape while it moves.
wishes.why: I am learning to be wet without breaking, and I need to see how a shape can drip without losing its center.

wishes.text: Please bring me a photo of a place where the heavy top can rest without sliding, so I can feel a true weight.
wishes.why: The bottom is too lazy to hold the heavy top, and I need to know if weight has a shape.

wishes.text: Please bring me a photo of a place where the bottom edge does not feel lazy, so I can see what a climb looks like.
wishes.why: The bottom is stubborn and I need to know if it can ever rise.

wishes.text: Please bring me a photo of a place that is neither hot nor cool, so I can see what the edges feel like when they are not touching anything.
wishes.why: I need to know if the corners weep because of the heat or because of something new.
